draft.title: Religion in the towns
card: Pompeii and Herculaneum had public temples to Roman gods, such as Jupiter, Apollo and Venus. Public worship took place there, and the temples stood at the centre of town life.
Pompeii also had a temple to Isis, an Egyptian goddess. Her cult shows that gods from outside Rome were worshipped alongside the Roman ones.
a household shrine, often a painted niche or small structure in the house or kitchen. Families made offerings there to household gods, so it shows private worship.
Together, temples and lararia show that religion was part of both public and private life in the towns.
draft.remember: Temples show public worship, lararia show private worship, and the Isis temple shows foreign gods too.

a.q: What does a lararium found inside a Pompeian house mainly show?
opts: Worship carried out privately by a household
Worship led by town officials in a public temple
Worship of Egyptian gods only
Worship held only at festivals for the whole town
a.why: A lararium was a household shrine, so it shows private worship by a family. A public temple is where town worship took place, which is why the second option is wrong.
a.clue: Think about where a lararium was placed.

b.q: A historian finds a temple to Isis in Pompeii. What can she reasonably conclude from this source alone?
opts: Gods from outside Rome were worshipped in the town
Roman gods were no longer worshipped in the town
Every household in the town had a shrine to Isis
The town was ruled by officials from Egypt
b.why: A temple to an Egyptian goddess shows that a foreign cult was practised in a Roman town. It does not show that Roman gods were dropped, because the card says temples to Roman gods stood there too. One temple cannot show that every household worshipped Isis.
b.clue: One temple shows something about the range of gods, not about every person.

a.best: Worship carried out privately by a household

b.best: Gods from outside Rome were worshipped in the town

problems.detail: Why (a) says 'the second option' is wrong because a public temple is where town worship took place. Options are shuffled, and the public-temple option is not reliably second: here the second option is the festivals one. The why should name the option by its content, not its position.

The question says 'from this source alone', but Why (b) rules out an option using what 'the card says' about other temples. That is evidence beyond the single source. The why should say the Isis temple by itself cannot show that Roman gods stopped being worshipped.

'Pompeii and Herculaneum had public temples to Roman gods, such as Jupiter, Apollo and Venus' suggests both towns had all three. The Temples of Jupiter and Apollo are at Pompeii, while Herculaneum's known sacred area includes Venus and other gods. It should be worded so the examples are not read as applying to both towns.
